Subject: Draft: tiered advance commitment + FY28 invoicing cadence

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a working pro forma that lays out two paths we discussed: (A) 1-year prepaid with a stepped discount based on token commitment, and (B) a 3-year committed model with increasing discounts and a staged ramp for utilization. Key points up front:

- We can provide a 10% discount at $250k prepay for FY28; 14% at $500k; and 18% at $1M+.
- For multi-year (3-year) we can layer an additional fixed-term credit: +3% year one, +2% year two (on committed spend), with annual true-ups.
- Invoicing: we support both a single upfront invoice and a fiscal-year split (e.g., 60/40 across FY28/FY29) to match your budget cycle — see sheet "Invoice Cadence" in the workbook.
- Ramp schedule: we recommend a conservative onboarding ramp (25% utilization month 1 -> 60% month 3) to avoid token overcommit, with automatic rollover buffers.

I've attached the pro forma and a separate sheet that shows the invoice splits and sample POs. Can you confirm: 1) whether procurement requires a single PO per year or a single multi-year PO, and 2) whether you need line-item pricing exposed for embeddings versus generation? Once I have that we can produce a final contract-ready pro forma and an official quote.

Best,
Ben

Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the detailed draft. A few clarifying items from procurement and finance:

1) We prefer a single PO per fiscal year; however, for multi-year deals we can accept a single master agreement plus annual POs.
2) Finance will need the invoice split to align with our FY28 (starts 7/1/27). So the 60/40 example you gave is promising — can you show a 7/1/27 start with the corresponding month-by-month burn/credit schedule?
3) Are the term discounts guaranteed against model upgrades (if Redwood swaps to a newer model family) or are they tied strictly to SKU names?

Timing: procurement expects a formal quote and PO request by 5/28 so we can get sign-off before our board meeting on 6/10. I can loop in procurement@alphaclinic.com if that helps.

Regards,
Elena Morales
Director of IT Procurement
Alpha Clinic

Hi Elena / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers inline below and I've attached an updated pro forma with a 7/1/27 FY start and month-by-month amortization:

1) PO approach: we can support a master agreement + annual POs (most common for multi-year customers). We'll include a contract clause to allow for annual invoicing while preserving the multi-year commitment discounts.
2) Invoice split: attached sheet "FY28_Start_070127" shows a 60/40 split keyed to your FY start — it also models a mid-year ramp so you can see consumption vs. prepaid credit draw.
3) Term discounts vs model upgrades: discounts are applied to the SKU family. If you elect to move to a materially different model family (e.g., standard -> large-family replacement), we propose a protected window: discounts are honored for the first 90 days after a model change, then revisited — we can add explicit language to the SOW.

Open items:
- Procurement wants the line-item breakout (embeddings vs gen). Karthik, can you please confirm the recommended per-unit SKU pricing columns and whether we should include a separate quantization/throughput addendum?
- Marissa, finance asked about an early-termination credit schedule and whether we can provide a guaranteed minimum availability SLA tied to this committed pool.

Next steps: I'll publish the redlined pro forma and generate a clean quote PDF if procurement confirms the PO approach by 5/28.

Thanks,
Ben

Reviewed the updated workbook. A couple of internal notes to align legal/finance before we hand it to procurement:

- Early-termination credits: propose pro rata refund of remaining prepaid credit on a 90-day notice minus an administrative fee (standard). If Alpha needs a non-refundability clause, we can swap to service credits instead.
- SLA: for committed pools we can offer a 99.9% availability SLO with defined remediation credits; for Dedicated capacity we can propose stronger SLAs but that changes pricing.
- PO language: legal prefers master agreement + annual POs with a quoted schedule in Exhibit A; avoid embedding monthly installments in the master unless procurement requests it.

Karthik: please confirm the SKU breakout and whether the embeddings price should be listed as a separate line versus bundled token credit. If embeddings are separate, we should offer an optional conversion table (X embeddings = Y token credits) in the pro forma.
